title: Reopen the SSE stream after the browser gives up on it (CLOSED)
body:
## Summary
When a reconnect of /events is answered with a non-200 or non-SSE body, EventSource closes for good and the studio stays on "Bus offline" with no live updates until a manual reload.

## Description
EventSource retries on its own only while readyState is CONNECTING; a reconnect answered with a non-200 status or a non-text/event-stream body fails the connection permanently (CLOSED). The Vite dev proxy answers exactly that while the API restarts under tsx watch: vite 7.3.6 config.js writes `res.writeHead(500, {"Content-Type":"text/plain"})` on "http proxy error". apps/studio/src/events.ts (before) only mapped CLOSED to state "closed" (watchConnection) and never created a new stream. realtime-events/push-vs-refetch-reconciliation: the reconnect floor is part of the design, and the shipped sse-reconnect-refetch direction (83a8846) only covered reopen-after-error, not a closed stream. Fixed: apps/studio/src/events.ts:168 keepConnected() replaces a CLOSED stream with backoff 1/2/4 s .. 30 s (reset only after a 10 s stable open - 76acd1d, stream-proxy-hop/reconnect-storm-hygiene) and the replacement's first open refetches active queries once (watchConnection `missed`, apps/studio/src/events.ts:125). Known deviation kept: reconnect-storm-hygiene asks for an attempt limit and a manual retry; here the one client re-dials a localhost API at most every 30 s and the nav says "Bus offline" meanwhile, so no storm and no green-over-dead.

## Flow
- pnpm dev; edit any server file (tsx watch restarts the API)
- browser reconnects /events through the Vite proxy while the API is down -> 500 text/plain
- EventSource readyState CLOSED -> Nav shows "Bus offline" forever; job/board/gen events never arrive until reload

## Expected impact
The owner keeps live job progress, board and generation updates across every server restart in dev without reloading; measured by the keepConnected cases in events.test.ts. Could break: a server that permanently rejects /events is now retried every 30 s (bounded, one request).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a closed event stream is replaced and the gap refetched
Before: CLOSED stream -> 0 replacement streams; 3 of 4 keepConnected cases red against a stub of the old behaviour
After: replacement after reopenDelay, one active refetch on its first open, backoff reset after open, stop cancels the reopen; 9/9 events.test.ts green
Method: gate - fake EventSource + manual clock in events.test.ts, seeded red first
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: 30bfc2c + 76acd1d (stable-open reset); apps/studio/src/events.ts:168 keepConnected; apps/studio/src/events.ts:125 watchConnection(missed); vite/dist/node/chunks/config.js:22004 res.writeHead(500, {"Content-Type":"text/plain"}); WHATWG HTML: non-200 or wrong Content-Type -> fail the connection (CLOSED, no reconnect)

title: Gate SSE event names against the server; drop dead project.updated listener
body:
## Summary
The studio's named-listener list mirrored the server's emit sites by hand with no gate, and listened for project.updated, which nothing emits.

## Description
realtime-events/event-registry: a mirrored vocabulary is generated or gate-checked against the artefacts both runtimes run; a listener on a name nobody emits fails as silent idleness. apps/studio/src/events.ts NAMED listed "project.updated" and an invalidation branch served it; git grep finds it only in events.ts. Fixed: EVENT_NAMES exported (apps/studio/src/events.ts:53); events.test.ts reads apps/server/src (non-test, comments stripped) for every literal emit name plus the SSE ping and checks both directions; job.* / gen.* families pinned to JobStatus / GenerationEventType.

## Flow
- server code adds or renames an event (e.g. emits a new board.archived)
- studio list not updated -> EventSource never dispatches it -> caches never invalidate; nothing fails
- after: events.test.ts fails naming the missing or orphaned name

## Expected impact
Developers adding a server event learn at test time that the studio does not listen; measured by the parity tests. Could break: a server emit written in a shape the regex does not parse is invisible to the gate (the 'found the emit sites' sanity check guards the regex).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one vocabulary, both directions gated
Before: 1 listened name with no emitter (project.updated), 0 gates; seeded red both ways (orphan listed; renaming render.done in the list failed the listener check)
After: 0 orphan names; 14/14 events.test.ts green
Method: gate - parity tests over the server source
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: git grep project.updated -> apps/studio/src/events.ts only (before); apps/server/src emit literals: board.decided, styles.updated, cases.decided, heatmap.updated, job.queued/started/progress, llm.event, render.done, + `job.${status}`, `gen.${r.type}`

title: Failure asks "is the API running?" even when the API answered
body:
## Summary
Every failed load showed "Is the API running on 127.0.0.1:8787?", including 409/404/JSON-500 errors the API itself returned.

## Description
async-ui-states/failure-states: name the cause you have; a remedy that cannot help misdirects. apps/studio/src/components/ui.tsx Failure rendered the hint unconditionally, while the server maps every error to JSON {error} (DESIGN.md Errors: app.onError). Fixed: apps/studio/src/api.ts:525 serverAnswered(e) recognises the API's own answer (serverError reuses it); apps/studio/src/components/ui.tsx:53 shows the hint only for a thrown fetch or a proxy page.

## Flow
- Board load hits SQLITE_BUSY -> server answers 500 {error}
- Failure: "The Board did not load ... Is the API running on 127.0.0.1:8787?" -> owner restarts a healthy server

## Expected impact
The owner is pointed at the real cause on every failed screen that uses Failure; measured by ui.test.ts. Could break: a non-StatReel JSON error body with an `error` key would also suppress the hint (no such proxy in the stack).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the failure copy names a cause that applies
Before: hint on 3/3 API-answered failures (409, JSON 500, 404); seeded red
After: 0/3 answered failures carry it; 3/3 no-answer failures keep it; 2/2 ui.test.ts green
Method: gate - renderToStaticMarkup test of Failure
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Remove dead shell exports, including a second status/licence vocabulary
body:
## Summary

## Description
status-vocabulary: one presentation table per vocabulary. logic.ts STATUS_META / LICENCE_META disagreed with the live tables (display.ts STATUS_WORD / LICENCE_WORD, glyphs TestChip): "DECLARED" vs "DECLARED · NOT TESTED", "Legal · monetized OK" vs "Legal". Removed: logic.ts KINDS, Kind, KIND_NAMES, MODES, LedStatus, STATUS_META, CELL_STATUSES, LICENCE_META, LICENCE_RANK, sourceLed, unlockCounts, BusState, busState (+ its test), STAGE_SHORT; ui.tsx SecH; glyphs.tsx Field, Kbd; base.css .field.

## Flow
- a future screen reaches for STATUS_META.declared.label
- renders "DECLARED" where Sources says "DECLARED · NOT TESTED"

## Expected impact
Developers see one vocabulary; -227 lines. Could break: nothing at runtime (zero consumers by grep, tsc and the full studio suite green).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - dead code and a duplicate vocabulary removed
Before: 17 dead exports + 1 dead CSS rule; 2 status/licence word tables
After: 0 dead exports; 1 table each; studio suite 34 files / 300 tests green
Method: gate - git grep -lw zero-consumer proof per symbol, then tsc + vitest
Result: better
Gate: none

title: One job-kind word table keyed by JobKind; gen_render had no words
body:
## Summary
Two hand-kept noun tables and one verb table for job kinds were typed Record<string,string> and each covered 7 of the schema's 8 JobKinds.

## Description
status-vocabulary/vocabulary-chain-integrity: a vocabulary is a type; a new member must not render as a raw token. logic.ts JOB_NOUN and projectState.ts JOB_LABEL duplicated each other (the comment claimed a cycle, but projectState already imports logic); gen_render had no entry, so nextAction would print "Job gen_render". Fixed: apps/studio/src/logic.ts:153 JOB_LABEL: Record<JobKind,string> (projectState re-exports it), apps/studio/src/logic.ts:137 JOB_VERB keyed by JobKind, unknown-kind verb "Working"; logic.test.ts walks JobKind.options.

## Flow
- schema adds a JobKind (as gen_render was)
- no compile error; Rundown/Studio show the raw kind or "A job failed"

## Expected impact
A new job kind is a type error until it has owner words. Could break: none visible (gen_render jobs carry no project_id today, so the words were latent).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one vocabulary, type-enforced
Before: 3 tables x 7/8 kinds, no gate; seeded: Record<JobKind,string> made tsc fail "Property 'gen_render' is missing" x2
After: 2 tables (noun, verb) x 8/8, tsc-enforced; logic + projectState tests green
Method: gate - tsc seeded red, plus a runtime walk of JobKind.options
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: packages/schemas/src/index.ts:318 JobKind includes gen_render; apps/studio/src/logic.ts:137,153; apps/studio/src/projectState.ts re-export; style follow-up e088857 (organizeImports blank line)

title: relTime rounds to "60 s ago", "60 min ago", "24 h ago" at unit edges
body:
## Summary
relTime chose its unit from the raw age and rounded inside it, so 59.6 s, 3599 s and 86399 s read as a full next unit in the wrong unit.

## Description
status-vocabulary/timestamp-display. apps/studio/src/logic.ts:316 (before) `if (d < 60) return round(d) s` etc.; relTime feeds Board tiles, the Rundown, Render & Gate and heatmap snapshot ages, and had no test. Fixed: the unit is chosen after rounding; every other age reads as before.

## Flow
- a Board item created 59.6 s ago
- tile reads "60 s ago" (and 3599 s later "60 min ago")

## Expected impact
Ages read naturally at unit edges. Could break: none (90 s still "2 min ago").

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no impossible unit values
Before: 3 of 3 boundary ages wrong; seeded red ("60 s ago")
After: 3 of 3 right; relTime tests + heatmap.test green
Method: gate - logic.test.ts relTime cases
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/studio/src/logic.ts:316 relTime; consumers: board/shared.tsx:387,553, heatmap.ts:119, routes/Projects.tsx:138, studio/RenderGatePage.tsx:49

title: Router re-declared the board read and the sport list
body:
## Summary
router.tsx built its own board query for the Board loader and kept a private sport list for ?sport= validation.

## Description
client-fetch-cache/portable-read-definitions: one declaration per shared read, warmed and read from the same place; one-authority-per-vocabulary. apps/studio/src/router.tsx: loader `warm({ queryKey: qk.board, queryFn })` beside workQuery.ts boardQuery; `const SPORTS = [...]` beside logic.ts SPORTS and schemas Sport. Fixed: apps/studio/src/router.tsx:204 warm(boardQuery), :115 asSport reads logic SPORTS; logic.test.ts pins SPORTS == Sport.options.

## Flow
- boardQuery gains a staleTime/select
- the Board route's warm skips it; or a new Sport is dropped from ?sport= URLs

## Expected impact
One definition each in the shell. Could break: none (logic.ts already in the entry chunk via data.ts; vite build ok).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - shared definitions declared once
Before: board read declared in router + workQuery; sport list in router + logic + schema, untested
After: router declares neither; SPORTS pinned to the schema enum
Method: gate - git grep count + logic.test.ts pin
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Bus offline state is invisible between 1100 and 1360 px
body:
## Summary
At 1100-1360 px the nav hides the whole connection tally, so "Bus offline" / "Connecting bus" never shows at common laptop widths.

## Description
apps/studio/src/styles/base.css:302-303 `@media (max-width: 1360px) { .nav__right .nav__tx { display: none } }`; below 1100 it shows only inside the open drawer. apps/studio/src/components/Nav.tsx:87 also carries role="status", which a display:none element never announces. A degraded dependency renders as though nothing is wrong (state-coverage). Fix: keep a compact degraded indicator (dot + sr text, or the word only when conn !== open) at these widths.

## Flow
- laptop at 1280 px; the stream drops
- nav shows nothing; the owner trusts stale screens

## Expected impact
The owner sees a dead bus at every width. Could break: nav crowding at 1100-1360 px (the reason for the rule).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - degraded state visible at every width
Before: degraded state hidden at 1100-1360 px (CSS read)
After: not taken - needs a viewport probe
Method: simulation - CSS walked at 1280/1366/1024 px; no browser driver in this round (no dev server allowed)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Playwright at 1280 px with /events failing: count visible nav text matching /offline|connecting/ (0 before) and nav overflow-x (must stay 0)

title: SSE invalidation grammar untested; calendar refetched on every job kind
body:
## Summary
events.ts invalidate() maps each event to the caches it refreshes with no test, and every job.* event (ingest, llm, audio, metrics) refetches the calendar although only publish/render jobs move it.

## Description
realtime-events/push-vs-refetch-reconciliation: surgical invalidation grammar. apps/studio/src/events.ts:73 invalidates qk.calendar for every non-progress job event. invalidate() is not exported, so no test pins the event -> key table.

## Flow
- on /calendar, an ingest job runs
- 3 calendar refetches (queued, started, succeeded) with nothing changed

## Expected impact
A pinned grammar; fewer refetches on the Calendar during unrelated jobs. Could break: a missed invalidation leaves the calendar stale (polling covers publishing slots only).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer refetches, pinned grammar
Before: 3 calendar refetches per unrelated job while the Calendar is open (read)
After: not taken
Method: simulation - three job kinds walked through invalidate(); the instrument (export + table test) not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: export invalidate; table test over (event, kind) -> invalidated keys with a QueryClient spy; count calendar invalidations per non-publish job (3 -> 0)
